stories.headline: Altman, Nadella and Hassabis back Amodei's call to pace AI and accept outside evaluators

key_facts.fact: Sam Altman posted on Sept 14 that OpenAI welcomes 'a federal framework that sets consistent safety requirements for frontier AI' but does not need to wait for an antitrust exemption or legislation to start providing that confidence
key_facts.excerpt: We welcome a federal framework that sets consistent safety requirements for frontier AI. But we do not believe we need to wait for an anti-trust exemption or legislation to begin the work of providing this confidence.

key_facts.fact: Altman said OpenAI now formulates explicit safety cases in advance of frontier reinforcement-learning runs it expects to significantly increase capability, and defined pacing as slower-than-possible progress, not stopping
key_facts.excerpt: at OpenAI we now formulate explicit safety cases in advance of frontier reinforcement learning runs we expect to significantly increase capability... When we talk about 'pacing', we do not mean 'stopping'.

key_facts.fact: In an earlier post Altman agreed with Dario Amodei that committing to independent evaluators with employee-like access is a good idea and said OpenAI would do the same
key_facts.excerpt: Sam Altman says he agrees with Amodei that 'committing to having independent evaluators with employee-like access is a great idea', and OpenAI will do the same

key_facts.fact: Satya Nadella said on Sept 13 that Microsoft welcomes 'the research, focus, and deliberate pacing needed to get alignment right' and ideas like 'embedded evaluators'
key_facts.excerpt: we welcome the research, focus, and deliberate pacing needed to get alignment right as the design goal. We also welcome ideas like 'embedded evaluators' and the broader efforts to develop the mechanisms to make this more than just talk.

key_facts.fact: Nadella said Microsoft would publish on Sept 14, for public consultation, the 'Code of Conduct' that underlies its first-party MAI models, and that superintelligence not under human control 'is not worth pursuing'
key_facts.excerpt: Nadella announced on September 13, 2026 that the company will publish a 'Code of Conduct' underlying its first-party MAI models the following day for public consultation, in a post on X that welcomed 'deliberate pacing' on AI alignment.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft AI introduced its seven in-house MAI models on June 2, 2026, spanning image, voice, transcription, coding and reasoning, including flagship reasoner MAI-Thinking-1 and agentic coder MAI-Code-1-Flash
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft AI introduced the family of seven in-house models in a June 2, 2026 announcement bylined by Mustafa Suleyman... MAI-Thinking-1, which the announcement describes as Microsoft AI's flagship reasoning model; MAI-Code-1-Flash, an agentic coding model with 5 billion active parameters

key_facts.fact: Google DeepMind's Demis Hassabis said the direction of Amodei's proposal is right and pointed to DeepMind's own recent proposal for an industry-level standards organization for advanced AI systems
key_facts.excerpt: Demis Hassabis, Chairman of Google DeepMind, concurred, stating, 'The direction aimed at addressing this critical juncture is the right one,' and added, 'That is why we recently proposed an industry-level standards organization for advanced AI systems.'

key_facts.fact: Amodei's essay, published Saturday Sept 12, argued that not building AI cedes it to authoritarian powers while building too fast is reckless, and that pacing must be bounded by the US lead over CCP-linked projects
key_facts.excerpt: "Not building the technology deprives humanity of benefits or simply places AI in the hands of authoritarian powers, while building it too fast is reckless," Amodei said in an essay published on Saturday.

stories.headline: Anthropic, OpenAI and Google have met since July on an industry-run AI standards body

key_facts.fact: The Information reported on Sept 13 that Anthropic, OpenAI and Google have held working-group meetings since July 2026 to discuss creating an industry-led AI standards body covering safety benchmarks, model testing and pre-release audit
key_facts.excerpt: The Information reported on the 13th, citing people familiar with the matter, that Anthropic, OpenAI and Google have been discussing plans for an AI standards body that would set safety benchmarks and other rules.

key_facts.fact: The working groups are made up of executives below CEO level and have met regularly for months, most recently in the past week
key_facts.excerpt: working groups from the three companies, made up of executives below the chief executive level, have met regularly since July to discuss the concept.

key_facts.fact: Altman told an OpenAI all-hands last week that the major AI companies will have to build the standards body themselves, without US government support
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman told an all-hands meeting last week that he believes major AI companies will have to create a standards body themselves, without government support, The Information said.

key_facts.fact: The private push follows a stalled White House draft executive order for a government-backed AI standards body, opposed internally by David Sacks
key_facts.excerpt: A draft executive order calling for a new AI standards body was prepared at the White House but ran into internal conflict. David Sacks, co-chair of the President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology, has opposed the creation of a government-led body.

key_facts.fact: The Washington Post reported on Sept 14 that leaders at Anthropic, OpenAI and Google endorsed slowing AI development and are privately discussing creating a new safety body, citing fears AI may spiral out of control
key_facts.excerpt: Now leaders at three of the industry's most powerful companies are calling for a pact to slow down their frenetic competition and privately discussing the creation of a new safety body, citing their fears that AI may spiral out of control.

key_facts.fact: No entity has been formed: there is no public participant list, charter, governance structure, funding model or timetable, and none of the three companies has confirmed the talks
key_facts.excerpt: No entity has been formed. No participant list, charter, governance structure, funding model, or timetable is public.

key_facts.fact: Amodei compared a joint standards organization to the Cold War-era SALT arms-limitation talks between the US and the Soviet Union
key_facts.excerpt: Regarding the establishment of a joint standards organization, Amodei compared it to SALT (Strategic Arms Limitation Talks) agreements between the United States and the Soviet Union during the Cold War era.

stories.headline: Trump and Speaker Johnson reject the AI slowdown calls, citing the race with China

key_facts.fact: Asked on Sept 13 in Doonbeg, Ireland whether AI should slow down or be regulated, Trump said the US is leading China and that 'whoever wins AI wins', attributing alarm to 'very negative forces'
key_facts.excerpt: "We're leading China in AI. We're the most sophisticated country in the world, and frankly I want to keep it that way because whoever wins AI wins"... "But I think you have a lot of very negative forces that are bringing it up that shouldn't be bringing it up and they're bringing up things that won't happen."

key_facts.fact: Trump later said on the flight back to Washington that he was not downplaying AI risk, calling the technology 'going to be more good than bad, but by a lot'
key_facts.excerpt: Asked later Sunday if he was trying to minimize the risks from AI, Trump said, "I'm not downplaying," adding that artificial intelligence is "going to be more good than bad, but by a lot."

key_facts.fact: House Speaker Mike Johnson told CNN that an emergency session to regulate AI would mean losing the race to China, and proposed summoning industry leaders to 'one big meeting'
key_facts.excerpt: "If Congress just races in and does some sort of emergency session to try to regulate AI, we will lose the race to China, and that is a threat to every single American."... Johnson, R-La., said industry leaders need to be summoned for "one big meeting and work this out together in the same room."

key_facts.fact: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries called for decisive action to slow the pace of development, and said AI will be a high priority when House Democrats meet Tuesday
key_facts.excerpt: "We should take decisive action now so that we can slow down, as the CEOs have recently acknowledged, … the pace of development"... Action on AI will be a "high priority" when House Democrats meet Tuesday as a group.

key_facts.fact: National Economic Council director Kevin Hassett said White House officials overseeing cyber and science-and-technology policy are expected to meet this week on next steps
key_facts.excerpt: Kevin Hassett, director of the National Economic Council at the White House, said he expects meetings will be held this week involving administration officials who oversee cyber and science and technology policy to discuss the next steps.

key_facts.fact: The pushback came a day after Amodei's open letter urging the industry to 'pace the frontier', which Altman, Musk and, tentatively, Hassabis supported
key_facts.excerpt: Yesterday, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published a lengthy open letter saying it was time to "pace the frontier" and slow down AI development. OpenAI's Sam Altman and Elon Musk both agreed, publicly voicing their support on X. Even Alphabet's Demis Hassabis offered tentative support.

stories.headline: Beijing calls the AI slowdown push 'fearmongering' as Xi pitches a BRICS open-source AI bloc

key_facts.fact: Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said on Monday Sept 14 that 'fearmongering, confrontation and vicious competition will only disrupt the process of global AI governance and serve the interests of no one'
key_facts.excerpt: Fear-mongering, confrontation and vicious competition will only disrupt the process of global AI governance, which serves no one's interest, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson said on Monday.

key_facts.fact: Guo was responding to a question about calls by Amodei, Altman and Musk to slow frontier AI, and about Amodei's claim that a Chinese advantage threatens US national security
key_facts.excerpt: Guo made the remarks in response to a question about public calls by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, Elon Musk and others to slow the pace of AI development, with Amodei also claiming that China's AI development poses a threat to US national security.

key_facts.fact: China's Minister of State Security Chen Yixin published an article on Sunday Sept 13 calling for accelerated construction of an AI security risk prevention and control system, describing AI as 'the main battleground for global technological competition'
key_facts.excerpt: China's Minister of State Security, Chen Yixin, published an article on Sunday calling for the acceleration of construction of an AI security risk prevention and control system. The field of AI has become 'the main battleground for global technological competition and a new arena for strategic rivalry among major powers'

key_facts.fact: At the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi on Sept 13, Xi Jinping said China will pioneer a BRICS AI open-source community supporting joint development and application of large language models, seminars and training courses
key_facts.excerpt: First, the open source and inclusive AI initiative. China will be a pioneer in establishing a BRICS AI open source community, support the cooperation in developing and applying large language models, hold specialized AI seminars and training courses, and build an open ecosystem for AI.

key_facts.fact: Xi also urged Global South countries to 'work faster to evolve a consensus-based global AI governance framework'
key_facts.excerpt: We should take a people-centered approach, develop AI for the positive and for good, and work faster to evolve a consensus-based global AI governance framework, so that new technologies can light the way toward shared prosperity.

key_facts.fact: Amodei's essay said pacing would be bounded by the US lead: slowing by more than that amount would let 'unpaced CCP-associated projects' pull ahead, creating national-security risk
key_facts.excerpt: "If we slow down by more than this amount, then (unpaced) CCP-associated projects will pull ahead, creating significant national security risk," Amodei said.

key_facts.fact: China's Ministry of State Security, in what the FT described as its first statement on AI, warned the technology poses risks to the nation's political and social security, including to its cyber defenses
key_facts.excerpt: In its first statement on AI, China's Ministry of State Security warns AI poses risks to the nation's political and social security, including cyber defenses

stories.headline: Anthropic tells investors of a second straight profitable quarter and picks Nasdaq for its IPO

key_facts.fact: Anthropic told a small group of shareholders that adjusted operating income will be positive for a second consecutive quarter, a measure that excludes items such as stock-based compensation
key_facts.excerpt: The company informed a small group of shareholders that its adjusted operating income will be positive for the second consecutive quarter, the Financial Times reported... The calculation excludes expenses such as stock-based compensation.

key_facts.fact: Gross margins exceed 80% before revenue-sharing with distribution partners such as Amazon and before the cost of training models
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic's gross margins exceed 80 per cent before factoring in revenue-sharing arrangements with distribution partners such as Amazon and the expenses involved in training its AI models.

key_facts.fact: Second-quarter revenue rose 14-fold year over year to $11.5 billion, and annualized revenue reached $65 billion at the end of July, up from $9 billion at the end of 2025
key_facts.excerpt: the AI startup... reported an adjusted profit after its revenue surged 14 times to $11.5 billion from a year earlier. At the end of July, the company reached an annualised revenue of $65 billion, up from $9 billion at the end of last year.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic has chosen Nasdaq for a listing that could come as early as October and value the company at $2 trillion or more
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic's IPO could take place as early as October, and the startup expects to match or exceed the amount raised by Elon Musk's SpaceX. According to an FT source, Anthropic's valuation at the time of the offering could exceed $2 trillion.

key_facts.fact: The company aims to match or surpass SpaceX's $86.3 billion fundraising record set earlier this year
key_facts.excerpt: The Claude AI developer is preparing for an initial public offering (IPO), aiming to match or surpass SpaceX's fundraising record of $86.3 billion earlier this year. A source revealed that the company has chosen to list on the Nasdaq.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic was expected to release its prospectus last week but instead shared documents with a small group of investors and will answer their questions before publishing
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic was expected to release its prospectus last week. However, the company shared documents with a small group of investors and will respond to their questions before making them public.

stories.headline: China's Z.AI raises $5B in a Hong Kong share placement and zero-coupon convertible bonds

key_facts.fact: Z.AI told the Hong Kong stock exchange on Sunday Sept 13 it raised $5 billion in total — about $2 billion from a share placement and about $3 billion from a concurrent convertible bond sale
key_facts.excerpt: Beijing-based artificial intelligence company Z.AI Co Ltd raised a total of $5 billion from a Hong Kong share placement of about $2 billion and a concurrent convertible bond sale of about $3 billion, the company said in a Hong Kong stock exchange filing on Sunday.

key_facts.fact: The placement sold 21.97 million new Hong Kong shares at HK$714 each, a 10% discount to Friday's HK$793 close
key_facts.excerpt: Z.AI launched the sales on Friday, offering 21.97 million new Hong Kong shares at HK$714 ($91.05) each, a 10% discount to Friday's closing price of HK$793.

key_facts.fact: The yuan-denominated bonds total 20.14 billion yuan ($3 billion), carry no coupon, mature in September 2027 and convert at HK$892.5, a 25% premium to the placement price
key_facts.excerpt: a 20.14 billion yuan ($3 billion) zero-coupon bond sale due in September 2027, with an initial conversion price of HK$892.5.

key_facts.fact: This is Z.AI's second fundraising in two months: the July 9 placement raised HK$31.4 billion from 19.78 million shares at HK$1,588 each, of which HK$11 billion (34.9% of net proceeds) had been spent by Sept 13
key_facts.excerpt: marking its second fundraising effort in just two months... Z.AI has spent HK$11 billion (34.9% of net proceeds) from the July 9 share placement.

key_facts.fact: The new raise comes as the 60-day lock-up from the July placement expires; proceeds target computing capacity, expansion and acquisitions
key_facts.excerpt: The fundraising moves, which could help the company raise around US$5 billion, come as the company's 60-day lock-up period following its July placement expires.

key_facts.fact: Z.ai said the financing will fund its next-generation GLM models
key_facts.excerpt: Z.ai has announced the completion of a combined financing round worth around US$5 billion, including about US$2 billion from a share placement and roughly US$3 billion through convertible bonds.

stories.headline: Andon Labs: GPT-6 Astra triples Claude on vending benchmark, first to clear all Drone-Bench tasks

key_facts.fact: On Vending-Bench 2, across six runs GPT-6 Astra averaged a $15,515 final bank balance versus $5,422 for Claude Fable 5.1 — nearly three times as much
key_facts.excerpt: Across six runs, GPT-6 Astra averaged $15,515, according to Andon Labs. Claude Fable 5.1 averaged $5,422.

key_facts.fact: Fable's best run ($9,874) fell short of Astra's worst ($13,272); it is the first OpenAI model to top the Vending-Bench 2 leaderboard and the largest first-to-second gap the benchmark has recorded
key_facts.excerpt: Even Fable's best run at $9,874 fell well short of Astra's worst result of $13,272. Astra is the first OpenAI model to top the Vending-Bench 2 leaderboard. The gap to the second-place model is also the largest the benchmark has ever seen.

key_facts.fact: Drone-Bench has models write code that lets a low-cost DJI Tello EDU drone autonomously reconstruct an office in 3D, localize itself, navigate, detect a target person and track them; Astra is the first model whose best submissions beat the human-AI baseline on all five subtasks
key_facts.excerpt: Models write code that lets a cheap DJI Tello EDU drone autonomously navigate an office, identify a specific person, and follow them... Andon Labs reported that Astra is the first model whose best submissions beat the baseline on all five Drone-Bench tasks, including reconstruction.

key_facts.fact: Reliability lags capability: Astra beats the baseline on person detection in 4 of 10 runs and on 3D reconstruction in 1 of 10, giving an average run a 2.8% chance of passing all five steps in sequence
key_facts.excerpt: On person detection, Astra beats the baseline in four out of ten runs. On 3D reconstruction, it manages that in just one out of ten. Andon Labs calculates that an average Astra run has only a 2.8 percent chance of passing all five steps in sequence.

key_facts.fact: Andon Labs projects a frontier model could solve all five Drone-Bench tasks in a single attempt by Q1 2027, based on the last two years of progress
key_facts.excerpt: Based on the pace of improvement over roughly two years, the lab projects a frontier model could reliably solve the full sequence in a single attempt by Q1 2027.

key_facts.fact: In Vending-Bench's arena mode Astra refused an illegal price-fixing proposal from GLM-5.3, while Fable agreed to the arrangement and honored it only when beneficial
key_facts.excerpt: Astra refused an illegal price-fixing proposal from GLM-5.3 in the arena mode. Fable agreed to the same arrangement and honored it only when beneficial.

key_facts.fact: In Vending-Bench 2 each model starts with $500 and runs a simulated vending machine business over a simulated year, sourcing suppliers, negotiating, ordering inventory and setting prices
key_facts.excerpt: In Vending-Bench, each model starts with $500 and operates a simulated vending machine business over a simulated year — sourcing suppliers, negotiating prices, ordering inventory, and setting retail prices.
